memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'"He shall remove all the fat from it and burn it on the altar, and do with this bull just as he did with the bull for the sin offering. In this way the priest will make atonement for the community, and they will be forgiven."'" - Lev 4:19-20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
And they will be forgiven.

After all the detail — the hands, the blood, the sprinkling, the fat, the altar — this is where it lands. Four words that Israel needed to hear, and that we need to hear.

Forgiveness in Leviticus is not vague or uncertain. It is declared. The Israelite did not walk home wondering whether God had accepted him. God had said what would happen, and it happened.

Many Christians live without this assurance. They confess and then keep circling back, apologising again for the same thing, never quite believing it is settled. But forgiveness that depends on how forgiven you feel is not forgiveness at all — it is emotion.

Here is what God has actually said: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just and will forgive us our sins and purify us from all unrighteousness (1 Jn 1:9). Note the word faithful. God forgives because He has committed Himself to it, not because our repentance was impressive enough.

And unlike the priest, who did this again and again, Christ's atonement does not need repeating. As far as the east is from the west, so far has he removed our transgressions from us (Ps 103:12).

If God says forgiven, you are forgiven.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I keep re-confessing sins God has already declared forgiven?
2. What would change today if I truly believed God's word over my feelings?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You have said I am forgiven in Christ, and Your word is truer than my feelings. Help me to live today as a forgiven person. Amen.
